Figure 1 has 17 distinct colored labels. Two are composite. All 15 single-gene signs agree with the registered coefficient and with the deposited group-mean ratio. The paper reports 2,639 fold-change-screened transcripts (1,731 up, 908 down) and tests enrichment at pathway level. No individual-gene RNA-seq test was performed for this follow-up. No gene was discarded on the basis of its registered sign or significance. Neither figure independently reaches the 30-pair v2 minimum. Their percentages are conditional on these selected pathways. The corrected proposal uses existing ledger values, keeps the compared closure for the registered contrast, and leaves fullyVerifiedContrasts empty.

The retained comparison assigns C3 only the 0.26–0.50 band. Figure 1 uses that band at (800,92) and (581,176) and 0.01–0.25 at (324,362) and (467,386), in original JPEG pixels. One positive sign is defensible. A unique C3 magnitude band is not.

The finding omits an internal inconsistency for Pomc. Figure 5b marks it significant and the Results explicitly describe significant RNA-seq upregulation. The Discussion describes a roughly fivefold nonsignificant increase across RNA-seq and RT-PCR, including the adult group. The Results assign the near-fivefold nonsignificant estimate to RT-PCR. The corrected comparison retains the printed RNA-seq star and leaves its point estimate unassessed.

The 2018 fold-change rule (>1.25 or <0.75 in Methods) applies to inputs for pathway enrichment. Genes depicted in Figure 1 include changes below that screen. Its 15/15 sign agreement covers the individually identifiable colored nodes, including those small changes. The paper also tested individual genes by RT-PCR, so the no-gene-test statement needs the RNA-seq qualifier.
